{{Short description|Type of linear operator on a Banach sapce}}

In [[mathematics]], more precisely in [[operator theory]], a '''sectorial operator''' is a [[linear operator]] on a [[Banach space]] whose [[Spectrum (functional analysis)|spectrum]] in an [[Open set|open]] [[Circular sector|sector]] in the [[complex plane]] and whose [[Resolvent formalism|resolvent]] is uniformly bounded from above outside any larger sector. Such operators might be [[Unbounded operator|unbounded]].

Sectorial operators have applications in the theory of [[Elliptic partial differential equation|elliptic]] and [[parabolic partial differential equation]]s, as they arise as generators of [[analytic semigroup]]s.

== Definition ==
Let <math>(X,\|\cdot\|)</math> be a Banach space. Let <math>A</math> be a (not necessarily bounded) linear operator on <math>X</math> and <math>\sigma(A)</math> its spectrum.

For the angle <math>0<\omega\leq \pi</math>, we define the open sector

: <math>\Sigma_{\omega}:=\{z \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}:|\operatorname{arg} z|<\omega\}</math>,

and set <math>\Sigma_{0}:=(0,\infty)</math> if <math>\omega=0</math>.

Now, fix an angle <math>\omega \in [0,\pi)</math>. The operator <math>A</math> is called '''sectorial''' with angle <math>\omega</math> if<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Functional Calculus for Sectorial Operators |isbn=978-3-7643-7697-0 |series=Operator Theory: Advances and Applications |year= 2006|pages=19 |doi=10.1007/3-7643-7698-8|last1= Haase|first1= Markus}}</ref>

: <math>\sigma(A)\subset \overline{\Sigma_{\omega}}</math>

and if

: <math>\sup\limits_{\lambda \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\overline{\Sigma_{\psi}}}|\lambda|\|(\lambda-A)^{-1}\|<\infty</math>

for every larger angle <math>\psi\in (\omega,\pi)</math>. The set of sectorial operators with angle <math>\omega</math> is denoted by <math>\operatorname{Sect}(\omega)</math>.

=== Remarks ===

* If <math>\omega\neq 0</math>, then <math>\Sigma_{\omega}</math> is open and symmetric over the positive real axis with angular aperture <math>2\omega</math>.
